3	- **R-7qd.** What a page lists, and what its story says, is only what the design changes compared with the app as it is now: a redesigned page the app already has shows its differences, not the whole page.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build*
5	  *proposed*
6	- **R-w3n.** A story is written only when someone asks for one; a design can be built without any.
7	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build*
8	  *proposed*
9	- **R-h8x.** The agent writes one story per page, and splits it only when the parts could ship on their own, saying why.
10	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build/stories/:group @ split-and-writing*
11	  *proposed*
12	- **R-b5k.** A story says it's out of date once the design changes after it was written, and says what changed since.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build @ typical*
14	  *proposed*
15	- **R-z2m.** Rewriting a story that was edited by hand asks first, because the rewrite replaces those edits.
16	  *proposed*
17	- **R-u6t.** A story is kept with the design on its branch, so it's reviewed and merged with the design; a person's edits are kept the same way.
18	  *proposed*
19	- **R-n4j.** A page's build session is given its stories, edits and all, and checks the build against their acceptance criteria; where a story and the design differ, the design wins.
20	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build/stories/:group*
21	  *proposed*
22	- **R-c9r.** A story never repeats what's already built: no built rules, no pages the app already has, and no rule from another page's story.
23	  *proposed*

2	
3	A redesign of a design's Build page (`/f/:folder/d/:design/build`): today
4	`server/views/_build.eta`, fed by `buildView()` in `server/main.js`, with
5	stories made by templates in `server/backlog.js` (`storyMarkdown`,
6	`incrementStory`, `layoutsStory`) from `increment.js`'s diff. The route
7	carries `"from": "@app/server/views/_build"`. The fake design being built
8	is "Loan offers" in borrower-portal (Offers, Compare offers, Accept an
9	offer, plus "Across the design").
10	
11	Pages: Build (`build/page`, its list `build/_pages`); a page's story
12	(`/build/stories/:group`: `build/story`, `_stories`, `_story`,
13	`_story-edit`, the `_rewrite` modal). States: typical, split and writing,
14	not approved, building, no app, all built. Event: `story-written`.
15

17	
18	- The story was raw Markdown in a read-only textarea behind "Copy as story".
19	- Stories were written for the server: route patterns, `POST … updates the
20	  record at …`, file paths; each card listed routes and "the design's view".
21	- Blockers (no app, not approved, behind main, building) were stacked cards.
22	- Old layout and ds/v1.
23	- Not only what differs from the app: `increment.js` compares with the same
24	  design on main, so a redesign of an app page (`"from": "@app/…"`) in a new
25	  design was "new" and got the whole page's story; a change on top of an
26	  unbuilt main design left the unbuilt part out; whole stories listed ported
27	  routes, built rules and every design-wide rule in every story.

text:
I've built the Build page, its pages fragment and Write every story. I couldn't run anything, so none of it has been rendered or tested yet. Prelude's next check is the first real run.

**Two things to know first**
- **"Write the story" and "Open the story" lead nowhere yet.** Their routes (the story pages and `POST …/build/stories/:group`) weren't part of this session. Until they're built, those buttons on the Build page give a 404.
- **Old tests changed.** The Build page's markup changed, so I rewrote the assertions in `test/build.test.js`, `test/app.test.js`, `test/increment.test.js` and `test/server.test.js` that checked the old page. I also added a test that writes a story, checks it's committed, and checks it's marked out of date after a design change. Run `npm test` before opening the pull request.

**What I changed**
- **Views:** `server/views/_build.eta` is now the page, ported over the old file. Its pages fragment is `server/views/build/_pages.eta`. The markup matches the design element for element; the only change is the partial's path, `./build/_pages`. `routes.json` points both routes at `@app/…`, and the page's `"from"` is gone. The page now uses the app layout and design system, not ds/v1, and the design's styles are in `prelude.css`.
- **Model:** `server/build.js` has the typed model, made from the states' shape. It also turns each page's changes into plain lines: new pages and overlays, which screens look different in which states, forms counted, and new rules and events.
- **R-7qd (only what differs from the app):** a redesigned app page now counts as a change, not a new page. If main's version of a page was never built, all of it is listed. Built rules and pages are left out. Design-wide rules and events now have their own page, "Across the design", and can be built like any other.
- **R-w3n (stories only when asked):** stories are no longer generated automatically, on the Build page or in the project page's "Copy all stories". Write every story has the agent write each page's story in turn, using `storyPrompt` in `agent.js`.
- **R-u6t (stories on the branch):** stories are saved as files in the design (`stories/<page>/…`), and each one is committed to the branch once written.
- **R-b5k (out of date):** each story records what it was written from. When the design changes after that, the page shows "Out of date", and the model says which change lines came and went.
- **R-c9r (no repeats):** the agent is only given the page's unbuilt rules and changes, and is told to leave out built rules and other pages' rules.
- **`story-written` event:** sent on the app's existing live channel each time a story is written, so the pages list reloads.
- **RULES.md:** I removed *proposed* from R-7qd, R-w3n, R-b5k, R-u6t and R-c9r. R-z2m (warning before a rewrite) is still proposed, because nothing built here rewrites a story.

**Where the design is silent** (also in NOTES.md)
- **Refusals:** the page has no place to say why a build or an approval was refused. I show the reason in the layout's notice region.
- **Pages waiting for the shell's layouts:** they still show Start a build session. Starting is refused with the reason, but the old page warned beforehand.
- **The shell's layouts:** they can be built without approval, but the button only appears once the design is approved.
- **Redesigns with nothing on main to compare:** these list "looks different in" every state, because Prelude can't compare against the app's rendered page.

**Before approving**
- Check the Build page in every state against its approved screen, especially the notices and the Building pill.
- Read `storyPrompt` and see whether the story format and the "never repeat" wording are what you want the agent told.
- In `groupsOf` (`server/main.js`), check the rule that decides whether a page is shown as New, Changed or Not built yet.

That label is correct, though it's easy to misread. It describes the whole design, not the page you're on.

The header shows "Approved · ready to build" until every page in the design is built. "Loan offers" (the design) has two pages:

- **Build**: built this session. Both of its routes now point at the app's views, its form needs no view of its own, and its rules are no longer proposed. When the turn ended, Prelude marked it built and cleared "Building".
- **A page's story**: not built. These are the routes under `/build/stories/:group`, the rewrite modal and the story editor. They weren't part of this session, so they still use the design's own views. R-h8x and R-n4j, which are shown there, are still proposed.

Because that second page is approved and still to build, "ready to build" is accurate. It will change to "Built" once a build session for "A page's story" finishes. That session is also the one that should make R-z2m true.

If the wording is the problem, I can make the label name what's left, for example "Build is built · A page's story is still to build". That label comes from the design page's code (`stageOf` in `server/main.js`), which belongs to the design-workspace design rather than this one, so I'd only change it if you want me to.
